hero.headline: Four suspects arrested in Martin County after armed robbery of teen and police pursuit
hero.teaser: Four people were arrested in Martin County following an armed robbery of a teenager and subsequent police chase, according to deputies.
hero.body:
Four suspects were taken into custody in Martin County on Monday after deputies say they robbed a teenager at gunpoint. The arrests came after a pursuit by law enforcement.

The Martin County Sheriff's Office announced the arrests following the incident. Deputies say the four suspects were involved in the armed robbery of a teen before fleeing the scene.

The pursuit ended with all four suspects being apprehended by deputies. The investigation into the armed robbery and chase is ongoing.

cards.headline: Byron Donalds skips Florida GOP governor debate, dominates discussion as rivals attack his absence
cards.body:
U.S. Rep. Byron Donalds, the Trump-backed frontrunner in Florida's Republican governor primary, declined to participate in the first major debate Thursday night, but his absence dominated the two-hour event. Former House Speaker Paul Renner, Lt. Jay Collins, and businessman James Fishback took the stage and mentioned Donalds by name at least 60 times as they competed to establish themselves as the strongest alternative. Moderator Patrick Bet-David opened by calling Donalds "the elephant not in the room" and explained that Donalds has raised roughly $100 million, polls between 48% and 58%, and will only debate once another candidate reaches double digits. Bet-David said he urged Donalds to attend but summarized his response as "Till then, I'm not showing up."

The three candidates attacked Donalds for refusing to appear. Collins said, "We don't do kings in the United States of America. We sure don't do them in Florida," adding that if Donalds wants the governor's mansion, "you've got to grow a spine, you've got to stand up, and you've got to fight for the people of Florida." Renner called Donalds' absence disrespectful, arguing that "every voter in this audience, everyone watching, everyone in the state deserves a debate." Renner said Donalds is avoiding the stage because he cannot prove he is better qualified. Fishback contrasted Donalds' fundraising advantage with his own ground game, saying Donalds may have made history raising money but "our campaign made history by being the first campaign in Florida running for governor to visit all 67 counties." Donalds told WPLG previously, "If the race was close, and we were battling it out, we would be debating right now."

The debate focused on affordability, property taxes, insurance, and hyperscale data centers. Fishback promised to take a "chainsaw" to local government spending and said he supports one thing only: "completely and totally abolishing property taxes in the state of Florida." Collins said cities and counties have "a spending problem" and need more accountability. Renner said the current property tax amendment does not go far enough and pitched his "Florida First" plan to eliminate most homestead property taxes while shifting the burden to tourists, out-of-state investors, and large corporations. The sharpest clash came over data centers, with Fishback promising to "reject and remove every experimental data center" in Florida and Renner pledging to call a special session to stop hyperscale projects. Collins urged local control with state "guardrails," prompting Fishback to mock his answer as a "word salad."

The debate gave the three candidates clips and contrasts, but the anti-Donalds lane remains split. Renner leaned on his record as House Speaker, Collins on his military service and role in the DeSantis administration, and Fishback on outsider energy and sharper attacks. With Donalds still holding polling, fundraising, and endorsement advantages, one debate without him is unlikely to reset the race on its own. Thursday night looked less like a campaign-changing showdown and more like an audition, with three candidates trying to prove which one deserves a one-on-one fight with the frontrunner.

cards.headline: Martin County deputies arrest 4 suspects in armed robbery of teen after pursuit
cards.teaser: Four people accused in an armed robbery of a teenager were arrested following a pursuit in Martin County, according to deputies.
cards.body:
Four suspects accused in the armed robbery of a teenager were arrested after a pursuit in Martin County, according to the Martin County Sheriff's Office. The arrests followed the robbery of a teen victim.

Deputies pursued the suspects before taking them into custody. The Sheriff's Office reported the four individuals face charges related to the armed robbery.

The incident occurred in Martin County. The investigation involved deputies tracking down the suspects after the robbery was reported.

cards.headline: Hobe Sound getting first Aldi grocery store at former Winn-Dixie location on Bridge Road
cards.body:
Hobe Sound is getting its first Aldi grocery store, opening July 9 at 8867 SE Bridge Road in the space where Winn-Dixie used to be. The store will hold a grand opening and ribbon-cutting ceremony on July 9 at 8:30 a.m.

The first 200 customers will receive a gift bag with Aldi products and a gift card. Aldi has converted multiple Winn-Dixie stores across South Florida over the past few years.

The Hobe Sound Aldi will be open daily from 9 a.m. to 8 p.m. The location is one of several former Winn-Dixie sites that Aldi has transformed in the region.

The opening gives Hobe Sound residents a new grocery shopping option in a familiar location on SE Bridge Road. The conversion follows a pattern of Aldi expansion throughout South Florida using former Winn-Dixie properties.

cards.headline: St. Lucie Mets Snap Nine-Game Skid With Late Comeback Win Over Tarpons
cards.teaser:
The St. Lucie Mets ended their nine-game losing streak Sunday afternoon with a late offensive surge, rallying past the Tampa Tarpons for a 10-5 win at Clover Park.

St. Lucie trail
cards.body:
The St. Lucie Mets ended their nine-game losing streak Sunday afternoon with a late offensive surge, rallying past the Tampa Tarpons for a 10-5 win at Clover Park.

St. Lucie trailed 5-1 after six innings before scoring two runs in the seventh and seven more in the eighth to avoid a six-game sweep. Tampa had been trying to become the first team to sweep a six-game series against the Mets at Clover Park since Minor League Baseball adopted the format in 2021.

The decisive rally came in the eighth inning, when the Mets sent 13 batters to the plate and scored seven runs on four hits, three walks and two hit batters.

Catcher Francisco Toledo delivered the go-ahead hit with one out, ripping a two-run ground-rule double off Jordalin Mendoza to give St. Lucie a 6-5 lead. Taylor Darden followed with a two-run single against Parker Seay to extend the advantage to 8-5. Antonio Jimenez added an RBI infield single, and AJ Salgado drew a bases-loaded walk to cap the inning.

Tampa appeared in control earlier in the game. Engelth Urena homered in the fifth inning to stretch the Tarpons' lead to 5-1.

The Mets' first two runs came on solo home runs. Jimenez tied the game 1-1 in the first inning with his third homer of the season. Branny De Oleo added his sixth home run of the year in the seventh, cutting the deficit to 5-2.

St. Lucie kept the seventh-inning push going when Jeremy Rodriguez doubled and Jack Scanlon followed with an RBI double off Mendoza, bringing the Mets within 5-3.

Mets starter Emilio Obispo made his second appearance of the series and allowed one unearned run over three innings.

The bullpen kept St. Lucie within range after Calvin Ziegler allowed three runs in one-third of an inning during a MiLB rehab appearance. Justin Scarborough allowed only Urena's solo homer over 1.1 innings. Caden Wooster followed with 2.1 scoreless innings, and Ernesto Mercedes worked the final 1.2 innings without allowing a run to earn the win.

Jimenez led the Mets offensively, going 3-for-4 with a home run, three RBI and two runs scored. Rodriguez went 2-for-3 with a double and two runs, while Trey Snyder finished 2-for-4.

The Mets improved to 3-10 in the second half and 36-43 overall. They are off Monday before opening a six-game commuter series Tuesday against the Jupiter Hammerheads at Roger Dean Chevrolet Stadium. First pitch is scheduled for 6:30 p.m.

cards.headline: Peacock House Art Foundation draws international artists to Fort Pierce's historic Crain Estate
cards.teaser: The Peacock House Art Foundation is transforming Fort Pierce into an artistic destination, preserving the legacy of Jaxson and Mary Crain while hosting artists from around the world in the Peacock Arts District.
cards.body:
The Peacock House Art Foundation operates from the historic Crain Estate in Fort Pierce, where Jaxson and Mary Crain once lived. Jaxson Crain was a tile worker by trade, and his craftsmanship is visible throughout the entire facility from the ground to the walls to the ceiling. Visitors can take guided tours of the lush gardens and vibrant architecture every Monday, Wednesday and Friday. The foundation says the estate is 90% the way it was when the Crains were here. The couple traveled the world nine times, collecting one-of-a-kind items for their Florida estate, including a gazebo shipped from India. The house includes a smoking and bourbon room with man paneling and a bathroom in manly colors.

The Crains are believed to have introduced peacocks to Fort Pierce in the 1970s, originally bringing in seven birds. The property now has over 100 peacocks. One peacock named Bob is believed to be 60 years old and walks with a limp. Bob lives in his own space with his own bowls and is hand-fed every day. The foundation's artist-in-residency program attracts artists from around the world, offering accommodations on the property. Art director Krystal Masters runs an art lab that offers classes for children and adults of all skill levels. Masters conducts one-on-one classes where people come in with zero experience and walk out with a piece of art.

hero.headline: Serena Williams withdraws from Wimbledon doubles with sister Venus due to knee injury
hero.teaser: The 44-year-old tennis star withdrew from the doubles match after suffering a right knee injury during her singles return earlier in the week.
hero.body:
Serena Williams withdrew from her doubles match with sister Venus at Wimbledon on Saturday due to a right knee injury. The 44-year-old Serena was injured during her singles return earlier in the week in a three-set loss. She posted on Instagram that she was heartbroken to withdraw from doubles and that coming back to compete again has been a gift. Playing alongside Venus once more meant the world to her, but her knee is not ready to compete. The post included images of four syringes showing the fluid drained from her knee after her singles match. An accompanying video showed her walking with strapping up and down her right leg and what appeared to be one of her daughters holding a cane for her. Serena was beaten 6-3, 6-7 (6), 6-3 by 20-year-old Maya Joint of Australia on Tuesday.

The Williams sisters, with Venus at 46, were scheduled to play Camila Osorio and Solana Sierra. It was the only first-round doubles match that wasn't scheduled earlier in the week, having been pushed back to give Serena more time to recover. Venus played in the mixed doubles tournament on Friday with Kevin Krawietz, losing in straight sets to Tereza Mihalikova and Lloyd Glasspool. The Williams sisters are six-time champions as partners in women's doubles at Wimbledon. With the U.S. Open approaching, Serena indicated she could play again somewhere else soon, saying to stay tuned to a city near you.

cards.headline: Argentina advances to World Cup round of 16 with 3-2 win over Cape Verde
cards.teaser: Lionel Messi scored his 20th career World Cup goal as Argentina survived a challenge from Cape Verde in a thrilling match that required extra time in South Florida.
cards.body:
Lionel Messi and Argentina beat Cape Verde 3-2 on Friday and advanced to the World Cup Round of 16 in a match where the tiny island nation challenged the reigning champion until the final minutes of extra time. The go-ahead score for Argentina was credited as an own-goal after Cristian Romero's header deflected off Cape Verde's Diney Borges in the 111th minute. Lisandro Martinez scored in the 103rd minute to put Argentina ahead 2-1.

Messi scored in the 29th minute for his record-extending 20th career World Cup goal, sneaking behind the Cape Verde defense as Martinez lofted a pass toward him. He took a quick touch and hammered a finish into the roof of the net past goalkeeper Vozinha for a 1-0 lead. Sidny Lopes Cabral and Deroy Duarte scored for Cape Verde with both equalizers stunning the pro-Argentina crowd in South Florida.

Vozinha had 10 saves against Argentina, including five against Messi. Argentina advanced to face Egypt, which beat Australia in a penalty shootout earlier Friday, in Atlanta on Tuesday. Messi has seven goals in this tournament and has 12 goals during his record eight-match scoring streak.

cards.headline: Saint Andrew's Scots football sets sights on state title after 10-2 season
cards.body:
The Saint Andrew's Scots football team is working through summer training with its sights set on a state title for the 2026 fall season. The Scots finished last season 10-2 with a district title but exited in the second round of the playoffs, leaving the team feeling more was within reach. Head football coach Jimmy Robertson said most of these seniors are four-year seniors who came from the middle school program. "They know how things are run. They had a lot of success in their career, and hopefully their senior year is the best season that we've had," Robertson said. The program is taking on a more challenging schedule this fall. Senior Jack Williams said the team wants to compete at the next level by playing against really good teams to attract new people.

For the Scots, improvement this season means one thing: advancing further in the postseason. Senior Jack Whelche said going undefeated in the regular season doesn't matter if they keep losing in the second round of the playoffs. "We just gotta go farther than that, that's all that matters," Whelche said. Senior Edmyer St. Jean said the daily summer workouts give the team something to look forward to. "Work harder so we can see the results when we come off the season positive and break our record," St. Jean said.

hero.headline: 18th Annual Treasure Coast Seafood Festival Returns to Vero Beach This November
hero.body:
Under The Sun Promotions, Inc. announced the return of the Treasure Coast Seafood Festival to Vero Beach for its 18th year this November. The annual event will bring seafood vendors and activities to the Indian River County community.

The festival has become a recurring attraction for Vero Beach residents and visitors looking for fresh seafood and entertainment. Under The Sun Promotions, Inc. organizes the event each year.

The seafood festival typically features local and regional seafood vendors, live music, and family activities. Vero Beach serves as the host city for the multi-day celebration.

The November dates allow the festival to take place during cooler weather along the Treasure Coast. Specific dates and venue details for the 2026 event will be announced by the organizers.
